11	Closing the perf gap in `kernels/fa3_hopper.cu` vs vLLM FA3 baseline on H200 (sm90). Started 2026-07-22.
12	Target slow scenarios (bench: `python -m bench.eval --set real` + hd256 fp8 configs from attntest).
13	Baseline geomean over the 12 targets was **0.735x**.
14	
15	**Iteration is expensive: each `bench.eval` rebuild of the 210KB kernel is ~200s (ptxas over all template instantiations, unavoidable). Batch high-confidence changes; use 2 GPUs (`--gpu 0/1`) + copied .cu variants to test in parallel.** Profile the prebuilt `.so` in `.fa3_trials/<ns>/` with `FA3_NS=<ns> FA3_CFG=<cfg> ncu ... python -m bench.prof_real` (no rebuild).
16	
17	Key FA3 mechanisms reverse-engineered (reference/vllm-flash-attention/hopper/):
18	- **Paged decode/prefill (page_size=1) uses cp.async, NOT TMA** (tile_size.h: paged_kv_non_TMA → kBlockN=128). FA3 hits 89% DRAM BW at the SAME 12.5% occupancy / num_splits=1 as us. The lever is CN=128 + a barrier-free page-pointer resolve (each thread loads 1 page_table entry, `__shfl` broadcasts across the 8 threads/row). Its num_splits heuristic returns 1 when batch*heads already fills the SMs.
19	- **fp8 hd256 uses RS-PV** (P kept in registers, MmaPV_is_RS=true), CN=128, IntraWGOverlap. Not a smem P round-trip.
20	
21	Changes that WORKED (in fa3_hopper.cu working tree):
22	1. Decode deep CN 64→128 (`DCN_D` for hd128 in launch_decode_split): decode DRAM 41→53%, geomean of 7 decode cfgs way up. **CN halving the tile count (per-tile softmax/pipeline overhead) is the win, NOT more pipeline stages.**
23	2. Barrier-free COOP gather (prefill_kernel producer): replace 2-pass smem-prefetch + `bar.sync` with per-lane page LDG + `__shfl`. decode DRAM 53→57%, s16k 0.72→0.81. **MUST spread the page LDGs across all 128 lanes** — concentrating on col_th==0 + shfl was 2.6x SLOWER (reproduced the old "serialized 2x" warning). [[fa3-cuda-eval-harness]]
24	3. fp8 hd256 → RS-PV at CN=128/STAGES=2 (build_P_rs_fp8/pv_fp8_rs templated on CN; drop sP smem tile; gated `RS=(HD==256)`). [status: in progress]
25	
26	4. fp8 hd256 decode CN 64→128 (launch_decode_split_fp8 FCN): 0.76→0.89x (mirrors bf16 decode CN win).
27	5. Persistent paged prefill: added a COOP-gather branch (`if constexpr(!USE_TMA)`) to prefill_persist_kernel + a paged persist launch branch, GATED to total_work<=12*num_sm (helps small-grid s2k/qwen +2-5%, neutral/regresses huge-grid s16k where per-tile HW scheduling is already optimal). Dense TMA persist path untouched.
28	7. **fp8 COOP coalesced gather (BIG win)**: the fp8 producer (prefill_fp8_kernel issue_load) was still using the NAIVE 1-thread-per-key gather (gather_row_k8_cp/gather_row_plain8_cp) = uncoalesced (32 rows-256B-apart/warp = 32 scattered sectors), pinning fp8 prefill at ~19k long_scoreboard. Replaced with the same coalesced COOP (TPR8=HD/16 lanes/key + __shfl page resolve), gated COOP8 (needs TPR8 power-of-2 dividing WG; hd96 keeps per-key fallback). hd256 fp8 prefill 0.841->0.917, decode 0.887->1.022. THIS was the fp8 lever, not just RS-PV.
29	8. **bf16 rescale-reschedule (FA3 schedule)**: our qk_rs_pv_g put rescale_o (64 ALU) BETWEEN the QK(i+1) and PV(i) wgmma issues, delaying PV and cutting QK||PV overlap (34% tensor vs FA3 56%). FA3 issues QK+PV back-to-back then rescales O AFTER PV. Added qk_pv_g (no rescale) + moved rescale_o_g to after wgmma_wait0 in both prefill_kernel and prefill_persist_kernel consumer loops; removed the epilogue pre-PV rescale. Online-softmax stays correct (O rescaled to running max at END of each step, ready for next step's PV). [measuring v10]
30	9. Async page-row ring (cp.async page entries into smem double-buffer, gather reads smem not LDG) — TRIED, REVERTED (s16k 0.73->0.475: per-tile pfull/pempty+fence overhead >> the LDG it hid on many-tile prefill). Diagnosis of page-LDG-on-critical-path was WRONG.
31	
32	**BIG WIN (v14): COOP gather TPR=8, not 16.** Matching FA3's kGmemThreadsPerRow=8 (8 lanes/row, KIT=HD/64 chunks/lane = 128-byte/1-cache-line bursts) instead of 16 lanes/row (256-byte/2-line bursts) lifted bf16 PAGED prefill 0.69-0.73->0.77-0.84x AND decode long-ctx 0.82->0.91x. The 15.6-sectors/req "optimal coalescing" metric HID this: 256B spans 2 cache lines and the memory system is far more efficient with 128B single-line requests. LESSON: don't reason away access-granularity; TEST it. (prefill_kernel COOP + persist load_kv_coop both TPR=8 now; COOP gate changed to HD%64==0.)
33	
34	bf16 PAGED PREFILL — earlier lever (v13): FA3 paged-prefill profile (device_kernel, ncu -k "device_kernel") is tensor 55.8% / SFU(xu) 29% at 1 CTA/SM; ours was 34.9% / 19.3% at the SAME occupancy. Cause: our PV emitted N SEPARATE wgmma groups (pv_box64 committed per 64-col box -> QK+PV = 3 groups for hd128), so wgmma_wait1 left only the LAST box in flight to overlap softmax. Fix: pv_boxes now wraps ALL boxes in ONE wgmma group (single fence + all pv_box64_body + single commit) -> the full PV overlaps softmax (FA3's 2-group QK/PV pipeline). Affects all bf16/fp16 prefill+decode. [measuring v13]
35	
36	bf16 PAGED PREFILL residual (0.69-0.73) — earlier ruled out structural causes: coalescing optimal (15.6 sec/req), NO register-serialization (C7512 warning only on hd192, never hd128), occupancy matched FA3 (1 CTA/SM), rescale placement matched FA3, 4 page-LDG-hiding attempts all regressed. Dense bf16 prefill (TMA, near-free 1-thread producer) BEATS FA3 at 1.03x; paged uses cp.async (128-thread producer, 2048 loads/tile). Both FA3 and we use cp.async for page_size=1; FA3's is 1.45x more efficient => residual is CUTLASS instruction-scheduling quality on the cp.async paged mainloop at 1 CTA/SM, NOT a structural/algorithmic gap. Levers exhausted without a further win.
37	
38	6. 1-tile page-row prefetch in the COOP gather — TRIED, REVERTED. Made decode/prefill ~1-2% WORSE: the page-LDG was already hidden by the STAGES pipeline; the prefetch only added register pressure. Confirms the prefill bottleneck is NOT the page LDG but deep mainloop scheduling (wgmma-wait + load latency unhidable at 1 CTA/SM), which CUTLASS's generated code overlaps better — a hand-tuning-vs-CUTLASS gap.
39	
40	**FINAL (working tree, ~v16/final2):** full 105-config suite geomean ~1.137x, 105/105 correct. Target set vs FA3: fp8 hd256 prefill 0.91 / decode 1.01; decode llama8b/qwen3moe 0.91-1.24 (CLOSED); paged prefill s2k 0.79 / s16k 0.84 / qwen 0.80 (up from 0.64, tensor now ~59% matching FA3). Additional wins after the fp8-gather + TPR=8:
41	- COOP TPR=8 (128-byte bursts) = the big prefill+decode lever (see below).
42	- pv_boxes single wgmma group (neutral, kept, FA3-match).
43	- WG0-only full[] wait (neutral, kept, FA3-match).
44	- Paged persist DISABLED (per-tile now beats it post-TPR=8): gate `&& false` in launch_prefill_t.
45	- Coalesced Q gather: v1 with real idx/rep div REGRESSED (0.79->0.69, expensive int-div 8x/lane). v2 with POW2 fast-path (real configs have rep=4/8, so token=ii>>log2(rep), head=ii&(rep-1) -- shift/mask, no div) is net-POSITIVE: s2k 0.794->0.813, qwen 0.812->0.820. LESSON: coalescing needs the divmod cheap; pow2 rep -> shift/mask.
46	- LPT m-block order (v20): the per-tile prefill_kernel dispatched causal m_blocks 0->tiles_m-1 (LIGHT diagonal tiles first, HEAVY last -> heavy makespan tail). Reversed to `m_block = causal ? tiles_m-1-bx : bx` (heavy first, light tail). prefill s2k 0.81->0.85, s16k 0.85->0.87, qwen 0.82->0.89. FA3's tile scheduler does LPT too.
47	- Persist re-enable + coalesced-Q reload: LOST to per-tile+LPT (0.78 vs 0.85) -- dynamic-FIFO barrier (~3082 pcsamp) + QBUF=1 Q-wait. Persist DISABLED.
48	- Persist STATIC round-robin (drop the atomic FIFO): WORSE -- broke the causal load balance AND regressed the DENSE prefill that shares prefill_persist_kernel (1.02->0.92). Reverted to dynamic FIFO + persist disabled for paged. Dynamic work-stealing balance > FIFO-overhead-removal.
49	FINAL prefill 0.85-0.89 (qwen near parity). Residual = light-CTA prologue (avg ~8 key-tiles/CTA for s2k causal, tensor ~43%) that FA3's continuous-ring persistent amortizes; my persist impl is too heavy to win.
50	
51	**SESSION 2 (2026-07-22) — root-caused the paged-prefill residual to CUTLASS mainloop codegen quality (MEASURED, not hand-waved).** Approaches tried + results (per-tile+LPT baseline = s2k 0.838 / s16k 0.874 / qwen 0.889):
52	- **TMA_Q decoupled from Use_TMA_KV** (FA3's Use_TMA_Q!=Use_TMA_KV: Q never paged -> TMA Q reload even when K/V uses COOP cp.async). Added `bool TMA_Q=USE_TMA` param to prefill_persist_kernel, tmaq_gqa reuses the validated dense-GQA 3D Q TMA box. Paged persist WITH TMA_Q still 0.78-0.82 (K/V COOP gather latency the single-CTA ring can't hide). Infra kept, branch DISABLED.
53	- **K-ahead-of-V (separate fullK/fullV barriers, FA3 IntraWGOverlap load)**: consumer waits fullK[st] for QK, fullV[pst] for PV; producer loads all K (publish fullK) then all V (publish fullV). REGRESSED per-tile (s16k 0.874->0.851, qwen 0.889->0.872): with STAGES=3 the producer already stays far enough ahead that V[i] is ready, so the split only added doubled __shfl passes + extra mbarrier round-trips. REVERTED. (Would only help at STAGES=2 like FA3.)
54	- **Paged persist PSTAGES=2** (FA3's exact kStages=2, 160KB): 0.62-0.64 — my hand-written cp.async ring STARVES at 2 stages; PSTAGES=3 (0.80) hides the gather better but still loses to per-tile. cutlass hides the same gather with 2 stages.
55	- **ncu SMOKING GUN (s16k, minimal wave-quant/tail)**: FA3 device_kernel (persist, 132 CTAs) = **74.83% tensor pipe util**; my per-tile prefill_kernel (4096 CTAs) = **60.91%** on the ALGORITHMICALLY IDENTICAL mainloop (same 128x128x128 tiles, RS-PV, QK(i)/PV(i-1) 2-group IntraWGOverlap, hardware ex2.approx, ping-pong). s2k: FA3 57.5% vs mine 47.8%. FA3 STALLS MORE (wait 1.99 vs 1.65, long_scoreboard 1.46 vs 0.39) yet computes more -> its warps are tensor-bound, mine are overhead-bound (issuing filler: addr-gen/pack/loop). The tensor-util ratio (0.81-0.83) ~= the perf ratio. This is SASS instruction-scheduling quality (ptxas/cutlass), and it manifests REGARDLESS of persist vs per-tile (persist can't beat it; even a perfect persist tops out at the per-tile mainloop efficiency). The causal-triangle light-CTA penalty compounds it for short-ctx.
56	- Consumer QK/PV ARE separate wgmma groups (qk_batch_g commits, pv_boxes commits) -> wgmma_wait1 correctly gates QK; schedule is correct. "issue QK(i+1) before rescale(i)" == old qk_rs_pv_g which was WORSE (delays PV, kills QK||PV overlap) -> not the lever.
57	
58	**COMMITTED (af89897, branch bench/sol-execbench-real-shapes, 2026-07-22):** the banked speedups (per-tile+LPT, paged persist DISABLED). 105/105 correct, geomean ~1.14x. Also updated bench/plot.py numbers + docs/per_scenario_speedup.png. Experimental persist-prefetch snapshot saved in `.experimental_stash/` (gitignored).
59	
60	**KEY INSIGHT (no codegen ceiling): my dense-causal hd128 per-tile mainloop BEATS FA3 (1.01-1.05x)** using the SAME schedule FA3 uses (verified via the FA3 mainloop extraction + my SASS: QK(i)+PV(i+1) issued together, WarpScheduler NamedBarrier ping-pong between the 2 MMA WGs, wgmma_wait1 leaves PV in flight during softmax's exp2, rescale_o after PV, deferred row-sum/norm; RS-PV, hardware ex2.approx, consumer regs 232 via setmaxnreg). So the paged-prefill residual is NOT the mainloop -- it is the 128-thread cp.async COOP producer's per-light-causal-m-tile pipeline-fill prologue (dense's TMA prologue is ~free -> dense wins; paged's COOP prologue is paid per light m-tile of the causal triangle -> paged loses). FA3 amortizes it with the persistent kernel.
61	
62	**Prefetched-scheduler persist (session 2, FAILED):** hid the contended atomicAdd behind the loads (FA3 prefetch_next_work). REGRESSED paged (0.72) AND the dense persist it shares (causal 1.05->1.00, gqa 1.01->0.96) -- for dense the TMA producer has no loads to hide the atomic behind, so the restructure only added overhead. The persist's measured bottleneck is barrier stall (ncu 1.46 vs FA3 0.44) = producer falling behind the continuous ring so the consumer stalls on full[]. Stashed. NEXT lever to try: make the COOP producer LIGHTER (less issue-slot contention with the consumers) or a dedicated lean paged persist; the shared dense/paged persist kernel forces compromises.
63	
64	**SESSION 3 (2026-07-22) — exhaustively tested the FA3-exact persist recipe; ALL persist variants lose to per-tile. Persist is a confirmed dead-end for this hand-written kernel.** A parallel Workflow reverse-engineered FA3's exact paged persist config (bf16 hd128 causal, page_size=1): kBlockM=kBlockN=128, **kStages=2**, **Q SINGLE-buffered** (FA3 has ~67KB headroom but does NOT double-buffer; the work-tile boundary serializes on Q in FA3 too -> QBUF is NOT the lever), K and V on **SEPARATE PipelineAsync<2> with K loaded one n_block AHEAD of V** (IntraWGOverlap at the load level), 128-thread cp.async producer. FA3 compiles 3 distinct kernels (dense-TMA / paged-TMA / paged-cp.async) at compile time; my single shared dense+paged persist kernel is the compromise it avoids. Measured persist variants (all vs per-tile 0.84-0.88):
65	- STAGES=2, QBUF=1, fused K/V barrier: 0.62 (starves)
66	- STAGES=2, QBUF=2, fullK/fullV split (K-ahead): 0.68 (K-ahead helped +0.06 but 2 stages still starve)
67	- STAGES=3, QBUF=1, fused: 0.80 (best persist; still < per-tile)
68	- STAGES=3, QBUF=1, fullK/fullV split (K-ahead): 0.77 (K-ahead HURTS at STAGES=3 -- producer already far enough ahead, split just adds fullV-wait overhead)
69	- prefetched atomic scheduler: 0.72
70	LESSON: the synthesis was CONFIDENT K-ahead would un-starve STAGES=2 to parity; the measurement said 0.68. Stages dominate; my hand-written cp.async ring needs 3 stages where cutlass's 2 suffice, and even STAGES=3 (0.80) loses to per-tile (0.87) because the HARDWARE block scheduler (per-tile, 4096 CTAs) transitions work faster than my software persist machinery (scheduler handshake + continuous ring + Q handshake). The templated-QBUF + fullK/fullV split code is in `.experimental_stash/fa3_hopper_kahead_persist.cu` (gitignored). Reverted to committed af89897. **per-tile+LPT (0.84-0.89) remains the paged-prefill ceiling for this implementation.**
71	
72	**Occupancy 2-CTA/SM (session 3, INFEASIBLE):** tried paged per-tile at CN=64/STAGES=2/MINB=2 (~96KB -> 2 CTAs fit smem) for cross-CTA latency hiding (the one lever the 1-CTA/SM persist can't use). HUNG. Register math: warp-specialized realloc = producer 40 + consumer 128/232 regs = ~38K regs/CTA; 2 CTAs = ~76K > the 64K SM register file. Warp specialization trades occupancy for register-rich consumers -> 2 CTAs/SM is IMPOSSIBLE for this design (FA3 also runs 1 CTA/SM). Reverted. So the paged residual cannot be closed by occupancy either. **Confirmed ceiling for this cutlass-free warp-specialized kernel: per-tile+LPT 0.84-0.89 on paged prefill. Levers exhausted: mainloop (beats FA3), persist (5 variants lose), occupancy (register-infeasible). The last ~13% is CUTLASS persist/pipeline codegen quality.**
73	
74	**SESSION 4 (2026-07-22) — banked a faithful win (COMMITTED fe7ee46); ruled out K-ahead again.**
75	- **WIN (committed fe7ee46): dropped the redundant per-tile `fence.proxy.async` in the COOP (paged) consumer.** The `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive -> full[]` completion already orders the gather before the wgmma (same async proxy) -- FA3/CUTLASS's cp.async consumer has NO steady-state fence (verified in the mainloop extraction). Removing it: paged prefill s2k 0.840->0.854, s16k 0.861->0.875, qwen 0.887->0.906; full suite 105/105, geomean 1.146->1.158x, now **0 configs <0.85**. Faithful, correct, no regressions. This is the pattern that works: find + remove overhead FA3 doesn't have.
76	- **ncu paged-s16k stall comparison (mine vs FA3 device_kernel):** tensor 61.3% vs 74.8%; barrier 0.73 vs **0.44**; long_scoreboard 0.37 vs 1.14; wait 1.66 vs 1.99; dispatch_stall 1.09 vs 1.12 (SAME -> inherent softmax SFU, not the lever); warps_eligible 0.80 vs 0.69. FA3 stalls MORE on loads+wgmma (productive, tensor-pipe saturated) and LESS on barriers. My residual = the +0.29 barrier stall.
77	- **K-ahead (separate fullK/fullV) RE-TESTED with shfl-once producer (no doubled __shfl): REGRESSED HARD** -- paged 0.854->0.710 AND decode 1.06->0.986 (decode's CM=64 path shares prefill_kernel). So the barrier stall is NOT the shared-full[] K+V wait (K-ahead would help); splitting only ADDS barrier round-trips + a worse cp.async issue pattern (fused interleaved K/V issue beats split).
